# Dust

A small command-line tool to quickly see which directories and files are using the most disk space.

Demo:

![Example](media/snap.png)

Overview

Dust prints a compact view of the biggest subdirectories or files. It automatically recurses into large subtrees so you can quickly find the biggest consumers of disk space. The display uses bars and colors to indicate relative usage and which parent folders subfolders belong to.

Usage

```
Usage: dust
Usage: dust <dir>
Usage: dust <dir> <another_dir> <and_more>
Usage: dust -p  (full-path - Show fullpath of the subdirectories)
Usage: dust -s  (apparent-size - shows the length of the file as opposed to the amount of disk space it uses)
Usage: dust -n 30  (Shows 30 directories instead of the default [default is terminal height])
Usage: dust -d 3  (Shows 3 levels of subdirectories)
Usage: dust -D (Show only directories)
Usage: dust -F (Show only files - finds your largest files)
Usage: dust -r (reverse order of output)
Usage: dust -o si/b/kb/kib/mb/mib/gb/gib (output format)
Usage: dust -X ignore  (ignore all files and directories with the name 'ignore')
Usage: dust -x (Only show directories on the same filesystem)
Usage: dust -b (Do not show percentages or draw ASCII bars)
Usage: dust -B (--bars-on-right - Percent bars moved to right side of screen)
Usage: dust -i (Do not show hidden files)
Usage: dust -c (No colors [monochrome])
Usage: dust -C (Force colors)
Usage: dust -f (Count files instead of diskspace)
Usage: dust -t (Group by filetype)
Usage: dust -z 10M (min-size, Only include files larger than 10M)
Usage: dust -e regex (Only include files matching this regex)
Usage: dust -v regex (Exclude files matching this regex)
Usage: dust -L (dereference-links - Treat symlinks as directories)
Usage: dust -P (Disable the progress indicator)
Usage: dust -R (For screen readers. Removes bars/symbols. Adds new column: depth level.)
Usage: dust -S (Custom Stack size)
Usage: dust --skip-total (No total row will be displayed)
Usage: dust -j (Prints JSON representation of directories)
Usage: dust --files0-from=FILE (Read NUL-terminated file paths from FILE)
Usage: dust --files-from=FILE (Read newline-terminated file paths from FILE)
Usage: dust --collapse=node-modules (Keep node_modules collapsed in display)
```

Config

Dust can read configuration from `~/.config/dust/config.toml` or `~/.dust.toml` to set default options.

Alternatives

- NCDU
- dutree
- dua
- pdu
- dirstat-rs

import pty, os, subprocess, select, struct, fcntl, termios
def run_pty(args, cols=80, rows=24):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    # set winsize
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0, 0))
    env={**os.environ, "TERM":"xterm-256color"}
    # also need to set COLUMNS/LINES? No

        try:
            r,_,_=select.select([master], [], [], 2)
            if not r:
                break
            data=os.read(master, 4096)
            if not data:
                break
            output+=data
        except OSError:
            break
    proc.wait()
    os.close(master)
    return output

for (c,r) in [(80,24),(100,30),(0,0)]:

// Config handling
use serde::Deserialize;
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Default)]
pub struct ConfigFile {
    #[serde(rename = "depth")]
    pub depth: Option<usize>,
    #[serde(rename = "threads")]
    pub threads: Option<usize>,
    #[serde(rename = "number-of-lines")]
    pub number_of_lines: Option<usize>,
    #[serde(rename = "stack-size")]
    pub stack_size: Option<usize>,
    #[serde(rename = "reverse")]
    pub reverse: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "display-full-paths")]
    pub display_full_paths: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "display-apparent-size")]
    pub display_apparent_size: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "no-colors")]
    pub no_colors: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "force-colors")]
    pub force_colors: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "no-bars")]
    pub no_bars: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "bars-on-right")]
    pub bars_on_right: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "min-size")]
    pub min_size: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "screen-reader")]
    pub screen_reader: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "skip-total")]
    pub skip_total: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "ignore-hidden")]
    pub ignore_hidden: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "output-format")]
    pub output_format: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "print-errors")]
    pub print_errors: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "only-dir")]
    pub only_dir: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "only-file")]
    pub only_file: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "output-json")]
    pub output_json: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(rename = "files-from")]
    pub files_from: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "files0-from")]
    pub files0_from: Option<String>,
}

pub fn load_config(path: &str) -> Option<ConfigFile> {
    // Check extension
    if !path.ends_with(".toml") {
        eprintln!("Ignoring invalid config file '{}': don't know how to parse file", path);
        return None;
    }
    let content = match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => {
            // For --config explicit, caller handles "doesn't exists" message
            return None;
        }
    };
    match toml::from_str::<ConfigFile>(&content) {
        Ok(cfg) => Some(cfg),
        Err(_) => {
            eprintln!("Ignoring invalid config file '{}': couldn't parse TOML file", path);
            None
        }
    }
}

pub fn load_default_configs() -> ConfigFile {
    let mut merged = ConfigFile::default();
    // Try ~/.config/dust/config.toml then ~/.dust.toml (latter overrides)
    if let Ok(home) = std::env::var("HOME") {
        let p1 = format!("{}/.config/dust/config.toml", home);
        if std::path::Path::new(&p1).exists() {
            if let Some(cfg) = load_config_silent(&p1) {
                merge_into(&mut merged, cfg);
            }
        }
        let p2 = format!("{}/.dust.toml", home);
        if std::path::Path::new(&p2).exists() {
            if let Some(cfg) = load_config_silent(&p2) {
                merge_into(&mut merged, cfg);
            }
        }
    }
    merged
}

fn load_config_silent(path: &str) -> Option<ConfigFile> {
    if !path.ends_with(".toml") {
        eprintln!("Ignoring invalid config file '{}': don't know how to parse file", path);
        return None;
    }
    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
    match toml::from_str::<ConfigFile>(&content) {
        Ok(cfg) => Some(cfg),
        Err(_) => {
            eprintln!("Ignoring invalid config file '{}': couldn't parse TOML file", path);
            None
        }
    }
}

fn merge_into(dst: &mut ConfigFile, src: ConfigFile) {
    if src.depth.is_some() { dst.depth = src.depth; }
    if src.threads.is_some() { dst.threads = src.threads; }
    if src.number_of_lines.is_some() { dst.number_of_lines = src.number_of_lines; }
    if src.stack_size.is_some() { dst.stack_size = src.stack_size; }
    if src.reverse.is_some() { dst.reverse = src.reverse; }
    if src.display_full_paths.is_some() { dst.display_full_paths = src.display_full_paths; }
    if src.display_apparent_size.is_some() { dst.display_apparent_size = src.display_apparent_size; }
    if src.no_colors.is_some() { dst.no_colors = src.no_colors; }
    if src.force_colors.is_some() { dst.force_colors = src.force_colors; }
    if src.no_bars.is_some() { dst.no_bars = src.no_bars; }
    if src.bars_on_right.is_some() { dst.bars_on_right = src.bars_on_right; }
    if src.min_size.is_some() { dst.min_size = src.min_size; }
    if src.screen_reader.is_some() { dst.screen_reader = src.screen_reader; }
    if src.skip_total.is_some() { dst.skip_total = src.skip_total; }
    if src.ignore_hidden.is_some() { dst.ignore_hidden = src.ignore_hidden; }
    if src.output_format.is_some() { dst.output_format = src.output_format; }
    if src.print_errors.is_some() { dst.print_errors = src.print_errors; }
    if src.only_dir.is_some() { dst.only_dir = src.only_dir; }
    if src.only_file.is_some() { dst.only_file = src.only_file; }
    if src.output_json.is_some() { dst.output_json = src.output_json; }
    if src.files_from.is_some() { dst.files_from = src.files_from; }
    if src.files0_from.is_some() { dst.files0_from = src.files0_from; }
}

pub fn merge_with_explicit(base: ConfigFile, explicit: ConfigFile) -> ConfigFile {
    let mut m = base;
    merge_into(&mut m, explicit);
    m
}
